claims.statement: The retry decision is a pure function of failure class, attempt history, subscription policy and an injected clock — the HTTP sender reports outcomes and never decides whether to try again.
Non-2xx responses are partitioned into retryable, terminal and throttled classes, so a 401 is abandoned rather than retried to exhaustion.
Retry scheduling is persisted as next_attempt_at in the delivery store rather than held in an in-process sleep, so retries survive deploys and crashes.
Budget exhaustion parks a delivery with the bound that was hit named in terminal_reason, and operator replay is the only path out — nothing is silently dropped.
A per-endpoint circuit breaker with half-open probing sits before dispatch so a hard-down endpoint costs a store write instead of a connection timeout.
